items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Yeah, we had to work with her, you know. ... I had to work with her for a while, see.

ctx.x: What were you saying about the Ann Cook record? I didn't get that, you know. About her phrasing and stuff?

Yeah, we had to work with her, you know. Get out on time and phrasing the blues, you know, on time. Oh, yeah. I had to work with her for a while, see. And Lewis being such a good monopolist. Lewis, the man, he was a great guy. He knew how to handle any kind of things. And he'd get in front of her and tell her when to stop and breathe. Pull her right in on it, you know, next phrase. And that's the way we got through them blues. She cut two sides.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Yeah, we had to work with her, you know. ... I had to work with her for a while, see.

ctx.x: 28th of March, 1963. That's right. And we're in the Seminar Room 2 at the Howard Tilton Library at Tulane University. And, uh, since you haven't heard this in a while, I want to play something for you. Recognize it? I want to see if we got the Ann Cook record.
Yeah, man, she's tough, man. That's the toughest woman in the district.
